title: Financial Maths: Hire Purchase, Simple and Compound Interest, and Exchange Rates
seo_title: Grade 8 Financial Maths Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems that involve whole numbers, percentages and decimal fractions in financial contexts such as profit, loss, discount and VAT, budgets, accounts, loans, simple interest, hire purchase, exchange rates and compound interest.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 financial maths worksheets: simple and compound interest, hire purchase, exchange rates and percentage change. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Simple interest is the same each year: I = P × r × n.
  • Compound interest adds interest on the interest: multiply by (1 + r) each year.
  • Hire purchase: total = deposit + all the instalments. It costs more than the cash price.
  • Exchange rate: 1 euro = R20 means multiply euros by 20 to get rand, and divide rand by 20 to get euros.

Examples

Example

R5 000 at 10% compound interest for 2 years

R5 000 × 1,1 = R5 500

R5 500 × 1,1

Answer: R6 050

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the depositAdd the deposit to the instalments.
Simple for compoundCompound grows on the new amount.
× or ÷?Rand to euros: divide by the rate.

A price changes from R400 to R480. What is the percentage increase?
